rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a promising baseline configuration. This experiment tests a multimodal model with PCA RNA encoding, ViT-L image encoding, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion—components that are likely to capture complex interactions between modalities. It balances exploration by using established encoders (ViT-L) and advanced aggregation methods (transformer), while avoiding overfitting through weighted fusion. This is the best use of the first experiment to set a strong foundation for comparison.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (ViT image encoder, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 58.56% accuracy. This experiment tests replacing ViT with ResNet50 (a simpler architecture) and switching to avgpool aggregation, which could improve performance by reducing complexity while maintaining weighted fusion. This balances exploration of image encoder alternatives with exploitation of the successful weighted fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows config_007 (resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6390). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method to transformer (while keeping resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion) could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of aggregation methods on accuracy, balancing exploitation of config_007's success with exploration of alternative designs.

The existing evidence shows config_007 (resnet50 image encoder) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether using imagenet_vit_l (a different image encoder) with the same RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion could improve performance. It clarifies the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, while building on the promising setup of config_007.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_007, 0.638999 accuracy) perform best. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer and fusion from weighted to concat, which could reveal if these adjustments improve performance. It balances exploitation of proven components (pca_n2000, resnet50) with exploration of aggregation/fusion variations.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_007 and config_026) achieve high validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the RNA encoder (from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200) while keeping the top-performing image, aggregation, and fusion settings affects accuracy. It clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choices in this setup, balancing exploration of critical design parameters with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows config_009 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation, a logical extension of the promising scvi_n200/resnet50 combination. It clarifies if transformer aggregation could further improve performance while maintaining the high-performing RNA/image encoder pair.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far. Testing config_032 (same RNA encoder and fusion method but with imagenet_vit_l image encoder) will clarify if switching to a more powerful image encoder improves performance. This is a logical extension of the current top configuration, focusing on a critical design choice (image encoder) that remains unexplored in this setup.

The existing evidence shows config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests scgpt as the RNA encoder with the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods, exploring whether the RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200) impacts performance. It clarifies if scgpt could yield better results with the proven image encoder and fusion strategy, balancing exploitation of current top performers with exploration of alternative RNA encoders.

The existing evidence shows config_032 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, exploring whether changing the fusion method could yield improvements. It clarifies if concat fusion might be better than weighted fusion for this setup, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with targeted exploration of a key design choice.
